title: Cohort-based embedding onboarding scheduler with safety gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: We onboard new open-source and fine-tuned embedding models frequently. Previous monolithic canaries expose high risk (either regressions in quality or hidden latency/cost regressions). Goal: build an automated, cohort-based scheduler that groups tenants by workload characteristics and stages traffic through gated steps with automatic rollback triggers. Scope: - Cohort classifier service that assigns tenants to cohorts based on query distribution (avg tokens, query type), dataset cardinality, and historical NN recall profiles. - Scheduler that stages traffic: dry-run -> small cohort -> broaden cohorts by similarity -> global swap. - Safety gates: quality thresholds (p@10 delta, MRR delta), latency SLOs (p99), embedding distribution drift metrics, and cost delta cap. - Observability and alerting: dashboards and automated pager thresholds. - APIs for manual overrides and emergency rollbacks. Acceptance criteria: 1) Scheduler can orchestrate a model swap for 50 tenants end-to-end without human intervention in test cluster. 2) No cohort sees p@10 drop > 2% or MRR drop > 0.03 for the first two broadening steps. 3) End-to-end p99 latency increase <= 10ms across cohorts. 4) Rollforward and rollback actions recorded in audit logs and visible in Console rollout timeline. Out of scope: per-tenant custom model selection UI (follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: E2E run for 50 test tenants completes without manual steps
No cohort experiences p@10 regression > 2% during step expansion
Automatic rollback executes within 3 minutes of threshold breach
Audit logs contain cohort assignments and decision reason codes
rollout_plan: 1) Dry-run: collect embeddings for new model and compute offline quality metrics (precision@10, MRR) vs baseline for a sample set. 2) Cohort A (low-risk small tenants): 1% traffic, 30m observation. 3) Cohort B (similar query distribution): ramp to 10% over 2h if metrics within gate. 4) Cohort C (large customers with stable distributions): staged 5% increments with strict SLI checks. 5) Global cutover when all cohorts pass. Each stage has rollback triggers: quality delta, avg cosine drift, norm shift, e2e latency, and cost-per-embed delta.
telemetry_and_metrics: Primary: precision@10, MRR@10, recall@K (K=10), nearest-neighbor recall at 1/10/50, cosine similarity distribution shift (KL divergence on binned cosines), embedding norm distribution, inference p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-embed cost, error rate for the embeddings endpoint. Secondary: downstream reranking click-through signal (when available), semantic search success rate from KPI tests.
automated_triggers: p@10 drop > 2% absolute for any cohort over 30 minutes
cosine similarity distribution KL divergence > 0.08 from baseline
safety_and_risk_mitigation: - Prefix / KV cache warmup dry-run before any real traffic. - For tenants with heavy caching, schedule swaps during low-activity windows. - Conservative traffic shaping for cohorts with high-cardinality indices. - Canary compute budget cap to prevent runaway cost. - Auto-pin to baseline model when persistent regression is detected. - Manual emergency rollback button exposed in Console with escalation playbook.
